question: Should `/v1/chat/completions` ever expose internal OpenClaw tool-call telemetry, and if so under what redacted opt-in API contract?
rationale: Current code and shipped docs intentionally scope `tool_calls` to caller-supplied client tools; changing that would expand a stable full-operator HTTP API and may expose sensitive internal tool arguments.

options.title: Keep Client-Tool Contract
options.body: Keep `tool_calls` limited to caller-supplied HTTP tools and direct internal-tool inspection to Gateway protocol, logs, or future observability surfaces.

options.title: Design Redacted Diagnostic Mode
options.body: Sponsor a new opt-in response/header/config mode that exposes only redacted internal tool telemetry with clear scopes, docs, and compatibility tests.

options.title: Wait For Concrete Repro
options.body: Ask for a redacted qwen request/response transcript before deciding whether this is actually a provider-specific tool-call bug.

recommendation.title: Keep Client-Tool Contract
recommendation.body: Keep `tool_calls` limited to caller-supplied HTTP tools and direct internal-tool inspection to Gateway protocol, logs, or future observability surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: They have adjacent follow-up history on the Gateway Chat Completions tool contract and are a likely routing owner for the API/security decision.
